land.text: Samarkand, Bukhara, the Fergana towns, Khwarazm, Balkh and Herat, taken from the Timurids between 1500 and 1507

predecessors.note: Tashkent (taken 1500-1503) was held by the Moghul khan Mahmud (eastern-chagatai-khanate) until 1503, not the Timurids; the steppe core on the Syr Darya had no state in the record.

land.text: the land between the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya, which Babur's defeat at Ghazdewan in 1512 'finally secured' for the Uzbeks

successors.note: The Khanate of Bukhara page dates the khanate from 1501 and treats Muhammad Shaybani as its first khan; Cliopatria and this project split the Uzbek state at his death.

land.text: Khwarazm, where 'in 1511 his garrison was expelled and power passed to Ilbars'
western Khorasan, Herat and Merv, conquered by Shah Ismail I in 1510
"all former Uzbek lands north of the Syr Darya" (Kasym Khan page), within Cliopatria's 1521 Kazakh shape

successors.note: Undated on the Kasym Khan page; the ledger carries it as a 1510 loss at confidence 1, the mirror of kazakh-khanate /ledger/6. The Kazakh Khanate page puts the border on the right bank of the Syr Darya, including Tashkent, Turkestan and Sayram, only by the end of Kasym's reign (Tashkent is the Khanate of Bukhara dossier's loss of 1521).

capitals.name: Samarkand
capitals.note: Shaybani took Samarkand, the Timurid capital, in 1500. The Khanate of Bukhara page lists no fixed capital for the early khanate (Balkh, Bukhara, Samarkand and Tashkent were its seats), so Samarkand is the researcher's choice for the dot. The page is silent on a seat in 1497-1499.

rulers.name: Muhammad Shaybani (Shayabak Khan)
rulers.note: Infobox: 'Reign 1500 - 2 December 1510'. His successor in the regnal table is Kochkunju Muhammad bin Abul-Khayr Khan (no dates on the page).

correction.text: the Shaybanid steppe core on the Syr Darya without Bukhara, which Muhammad Shaybani 'conquered ... in 1501'

keyframe_review.note: 395,934 km2: the Syr Darya steppe from Turkestan to Qyzylorda plus Bukhara. Shaybani 'conquered Bukhara in 1501', so Bukhara is removed for 1497-1500 and added by the 1501 event; Samarkand (1500) is added by the 1500 event. The steppe core is the Kazakh Khanate page's division of c. 1495-96 ("the Shaybanids held the southern cities such as Otrar, Yasi, Arkuq, and Uzgend"); the Muhammad Shaybani page dates his reign from 1500 and the Burunduk Khan page is silent. No infobox area exists to compare.

686,520 km2: Transoxiana with Samarkand, Bukhara, Tashkent, Fergana and Khujand. The Khanate of Bukhara page has Bukhara, Samarkand, Tashkent and Andijan fall to Shaybani 'from 1500 to 1503', so the shape (from 1502) is inside that span; the ledger carries the dated steps (Samarkand 1500, Bukhara 1501, the rest 1502).

correction.text: the shape for 1507-1509 only: 'In 1501 he recaptured Samarkand and in 1507 also took Herat', without the southern tongue (Birjand, Zabol) on Mihrabanid Sistan and Quhistan; years shortened

keyframe_review.note: 1,747,804 km2 for 1507-1511: Transoxiana, Khwarazm (1505), Balkh (1506), Herat and Khorasan (1507) and a southern tongue to 30.6 N (Birjand, Zabol) that no opened page supports (repair round: the Herat page, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herat, says only 'In 1507, Herat was occupied by the Uzbeks' and 'taken by Shah Isma'il ... in 1510', and names no Birjand, Zabol or Sistan; the tongue stays as Cliopatria's unverified outline, soft). The shape is right for 1507-1509 only (its 707 Kazakhstan cells go to Kasym in 1510, see the 1510 loss): Shaybani was killed outside Merv on 2 December 1510 and Ismail I took Khorasan in 1510, so 1510 and 1511 are given by two new keyframes. The pages give no area to compare. Fix fx-31 (F287): the southern tongue to 30.6 N is now subtracted (Sistan and South Khorasan, 396 cells, the conflict with mihrabanids in 1507, 1510 and 1511): the Mihrabanids page has the Mihrabanids as Timurid vassals 'until the latter's overthrow by the Shaybanids' and then, in 'the early 16th century', 'Malik Sultan Mahmud became a Safavid vassal'; it never has the Uzbeks holding Sistan, and the Muhammad Shaybani page names no Sistan, Birjand or Zabol.

correction.text: the 1507 shape without Khorasan, Herat, Merv and Balkh, lost to Shah Ismail I in 1510, and without the Syr Darya lands north of the river that the Uzbeks gave to Kasym (bridged to 1510), and without Sistan and Quhistan (Mihrabanid land, fx-31)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1510: Ismail I invaded Khorasan, took Astrabad, Mashhad and Sarakhs and killed Shaybani at Merv; Balkh was 'briefly expelled by the Safavids in 1510'. The Uzbek state keeps Transoxiana and Khwarazm. Kazakh Khanate page: "In 1510, however, Kasym Khan inflicted a major defeat on a large Uzbek force"; the Kasym Khan page has the Uzbeks give Kasym 'all former Uzbek lands north of the Syr Darya' (undated; ledger 1510 loss at confidence 1). (Repair round ia-03-b, 2026-10-19: steppe removed.) Fix fx-31 (F287): Sistan and South Khorasan are subtracted too (the Mihrabanids page gives no Uzbek rule there).

correction.text: the 1507 shape without Khorasan, Herat, Merv, Balkh, Khwarazm, the Syr Darya lands north of the river, and Samarkand and Bukhara: Transoxiana less the two cities Babur held in 1511, and without Sistan and Quhistan (Mihrabanid land, fx-31)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1511, the last year of the Shaybanid row: Khwarazm, 'shortly occupied' by Shah Ismail after Merv (December 1510), whose garrison was expelled in 1511 when 'power passed to Ilbars' (the Khanate of Khiva); Babur ruled Balkh as a Safavid vassal in 1511-1512 (Balkh page). Samarkand and Bukhara are Babur's in 1511: the Babur page has him 'take Samarkand for the third time' ("Thus, in 1511") and 'also took Bukhara but lost both again to the Uzbeks in 1512', with no month, so the yearly keyframe drops both; the Uzbeks recover them in 1512 and the Khanate of Bukhara dossier carries on from 1512. What is left is Transoxiana without the two cities. (Repair round ia-03-b, 2026-10-19: Samarkand and Bukhara removed.) Fix fx-31 (F287): Sistan and South Khorasan are subtracted too (the Mihrabanids page gives no Uzbek rule there).

region.text: the Syr Darya steppe holdings of the division of c. 1495-96 (Otrar, Yasi/Turkestan, Arkuq, Uzgend): the 680 Kazakhstan cells of Cliopatria's 1497 shape, without Bukhara

ledger.note: 1497: the Shaybanid holdings on the Syr Darya, the first Shaybanid shape in Cliopatria. The Kazakh Khanate page: "Around 1495-1496, Burunduk Khan and Muhammad Shaybani Khan agreed on a division of territories", "while the Shaybanids held the southern cities such as Otrar, Yasi, Arkuq, and Uzgend". kazakh-khanate /ledger/5 dates the loss of these same 680 cells 1496; this dossier keeps Cliopatria's first-shape year, 1497, as its start, so 1496 is one year in which the pages' division has no owner on the map. The region is Cliopatria's cells, not the page's boundary (the page names cities only), hence confidence 2. The Burunduk Khan page (opened in the repair round) names no division, city or year; the Muhammad Shaybani page dates his reign from 1500 (infobox 'Reign: 1500 - 2 December 1510'). (Repair round ia-03-b, 2026-10-19: was counterpart nobody, confidence 1, region the two provinces South Kazakhstan and Qyzylorda, source Muhammad Shaybani.)
1500: Shaybani takes Samarkand from the Timurids. 'Shaybani ousted the Timurids from their capital Samarkand in 1500.'

1501: Shaybani conquers Bukhara. 'Shaybani conquered Bukhara in 1501'; the same page says 'In 1501 he recaptured Samarkand', and the Khanate of Bukhara page adds the Battle of Sar-i Pul in the spring of 1501.

region.text: Andijan and the Fergana towns, with Khujand

ledger.note: 1502: Fergana and Khujand pass to the Uzbeks. The Khanate of Bukhara page has Bukhara, Samarkand, Tashkent and Andijan fall 'from 1500 to 1503'; the year 1502 is Cliopatria's (the shape that first holds them), not the page's. Andijan was Timurid (Cliopatria's Timurid shape of 1497-1501 holds Fergana). Repair round ia-03-b, 2026-10-19: the Babur page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babur) says only that in 1501 he 'briefly recaptured' Samarkand and Fergana and that "By 1502, he had resigned all hopes of recovering Fergana"; it names no Uzbek conquest of Fergana, does not mention Khujand and gives no year for it, so the year stays Cliopatria's, at confidence 1. timurid-empire /ledger/44 carries Fergana in its 1501 loss, one year earlier.

1503: Tashkent falls to the Uzbeks. The Moghulistan page has Mahmud Khan as 'the ruler of western Moghulistan in Tashkent'; in 1503 Ahmad Alaq 'traveled west to assist his brother' against Muhammad Shaybani: 'The brothers were defeated and captured; they were released but Tashkent was seized by the Uzbeks.' Mahmud's Tashkent realm is the eastern-chagatai-khanate dossier, which records the same loss in 1503. (Reviewer ia-03-b, 2026-10-19: was 1502, counterpart moghulistan, confidence 1, source Khanate_of_Bukhara; moghulistan's own ledger hands Tashkent to eastern-chagatai-khanate in 1492.)

1505: Shaybani takes Urgench after a ten-month siege and annexes Khwarazm. 'In 1505 Muhammad Shaybani took Urgench after a 10-month siege.' The page names no ruler; the Khanate of Khiva page lists the Timurid Empire as its predecessor.
1506: Balkh falls to the Uzbeks. The Uzbeks took the city in 1506 under Muhammad Shaybani (the Khanate of Bukhara page: 'In 1506 Shaybani captured Balkh').

region.text: Herat, Khorasan and Kunduz; Sistan and Quhistan (South Khorasan) left to the Mihrabanids

ledger.note: 1507: Herat and Khorasan fall. 'Finally in 1507 he was able to take Herat', along with Kunduz and Khorasan (the Muhammad Shaybani page: 'in 1507 also took Herat'). The page names no Khorasan towns beyond Herat; Cliopatria's 1507 shape adds Mashhad, Gorgan and the south. Fix fx-31 (F287): Quhistan (South Khorasan) and Sistan are not in this gain: the Mihrabanids page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mihrabanids) has Malik Sultan Mahmud, a Timurid vassal, become 'a Safavid vassal' in the early 16th century and names no Uzbek rule.
1510: Ismail I invades Khorasan. 'In 1510, Shaybani Khan was in Herat'; Ismail then invaded western Khorasan, took Astrabad, Mashhad and Sarakhs and besieged Merv for a month.
1510: Balkh is lost. The Uzbeks were 'briefly expelled by the Safavids in 1510'; Babur then ruled it as a Safavid vassal in 1511-1512 until Bukhara defeated him.

region.text: the Uzbek lands north of the Syr Darya, within Cliopatria's 1521 Kazakh shape (the 669 cells kazakh-khanate gains)

ledger.note: 1510: the Uzbeks give up the Syr Darya lands north of the river to Kasym. Kasym Khan page: "After Shaybani and the Uzbeks suffered severe losses in numerous battles near Lake Balkhash," "the Uzbek Khanate agreed to give Qasim Khan and the Kazakhs all former Uzbek lands north of the Syr Darya"; the page gives no year for the handover and says Qasim fought Shaybani "Shortly after taking the throne in 1510". The Kazakh Khanate page has "In 1510, however, Kasym Khan inflicted a major defeat on a large Uzbek force", and Shaybani was killed on 2 December 1510 (Muhammad Shaybani page), so 1510 is bridged, at confidence 1, as in kazakh-khanate /ledger/6, whose region this copies. The Kazakh Khanate page also puts the Kazakh border on the right bank of the Syr Darya 'including Tashkent, Turkestan, and Sayram' only 'by the end of Kasym Khan's reign'. (Repair round ia-03-b, 2026-10-19: new event, the mirror of kazakh-khanate /ledger/6.)
2 December 1510: Muhammad Shaybani is killed at Merv. 'In the Battle of Marv (1510), Muhammad Shaybani was defeated and killed when trying to escape'; the Safavids hold Khorasan.
December 1510: Khorasan, Herat and Merv pass to the Safavids after Merv; the Merv page also has Ismail expel the Uzbeks from Merv in 1510.

December 1510: Khwarazm passes to the Safavids after Merv. The Khanate of Khiva page: Shah Ismail I and Muhammad Shaybani 'clashed in 1510 near Merv with Muhammad killed in the battle and Khorezm shortly occupied. The Shah's religion provoked resistance and in 1511 his garrison was expelled and power passed to Ilbars'. The month follows the battle (2 December 1510); 'shortly' may mean early 1511. (Reviewer ia-03-b, 2026-10-19: was a 1511 loss to khanate-of-khiva at confidence 3; the garrison expelled in 1511 was the Shah's, not Shaybani's.)

1511: Babur takes Samarkand and Bukhara from the Uzbeks. Babur page: "Thus, in 1511" "he managed to take Samarkand for the third time"; "he also took Bukhara but lost both again to the Uzbeks in 1512." The page gives no month, so the Uzbek shape of 1511 (a yearly keyframe) drops both cities; the Uzbeks recover them in 1512 (Ghazdewan), which khanate-of-bukhara records. The mirror of timurid-empire /ledger/48, whose region this copies. (Repair round ia-03-b, 2026-10-19: new event; the dossier had no 1511 event for Babur.)

region.text: what remained of the Uzbek state at the end of 1511: Transoxiana without Samarkand and Bukhara, which Babur held in 1511

ledger.note: 1511: the Shaybanid empire ends with Transoxiana left to the Uzbek khans of Bukhara and Samarkand, less the two cities Babur held in 1511 (the loss above). Muhammad Shaybani died on 2 December 1510; Babur "also took Bukhara but lost both again to the Uzbeks in 1512" (Babur page), after which the Uzbeks held Transoxiana. The Khanate of Bukhara page dates the khanate from 1501; this project closes the Shaybanid row at its Cliopatria end and opens Bukhara in 1512. (Repair round ia-03-b, 2026-10-19: the Babur page dates the capture to 1511, not 1512; region now excludes the two cities.)

wars.name: Shaybanid conquest of Transoxiana, Khwarazm and Khorasan

zones.text: Samarkand 1500, Bukhara 1501, Tashkent and Andijan 1500-1503, Urgench 1505, Balkh 1506, Herat 1507

wars.outcome: Shaybani ousts the Timurids from Samarkand (1500), takes Bukhara (1501), Urgench (1505), Balkh (1506) and Herat (1507).

wars.name: Shaybanid-Safavid war and the Battle of Merv
wars.outcome: Ismail I invades Khorasan, besieges Merv for a month and defeats and kills Shaybani there (2 December 1510); the Safavids keep Khorasan.

wars.name: Shaybanid-Kazakh border raids
wars.outcome: Shaybani raided northwards in 1508-1509, 'pillaging the land of the Kazakh Khanate'; in 1510 Kasym Khan 'inflicted a major defeat on a large Uzbek force'. No border is dated.
wars.note: The Muhammad Shaybani page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Shaybani) gives the 1508-09 raids; the Kazakh Khanate page gives the 1510 defeat and says 'the southern borders of the Kazakh Khanate extended to the right bank of the Syr Darya, including Tashkent, Turkestan and Sayram' by the end of Kasym's reign. Repair round ia-03-b, 2026-10-19: the Kasym Khan page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasym_Khan) adds that after the Uzbeks 'suffered severe losses in numerous battles near Lake Balkhash' the Uzbek Khanate 'agreed to give Qasim Khan and the Kazakhs all former Uzbek lands north of the Syr Darya' (undated; the ledger bridges it to 1510 at confidence 1).

certainty.note: A steppe and oasis empire: city holdings are known, frontiers between them are not surveyed. Nothing here is a treaty line.

notes:
Shaybanids: 1497..1511, 3 Cliopatria shapes; 2 pages budgeted, 7 opened because the events need them (Muhammad Shaybani, Shaybanids, Khanate of Bukhara, Balkh, Khanate of Khiva, Kazakh Khanate, Moghulistan; the first six are also in the Bukhara and Khiva dossiers) and 4 more in the repair round of 2026-10-19 (Babur, Kasym Khan, Burunduk Khan, Herat).
Cliopatria seam: the Khanate of Bukhara page dates the khanate from 1501 and treats Muhammad Shaybani as its first khan; Cliopatria has Shaybanids 1497-1511, Khiva from 1512 and Bukhara from 1516 (different Wikidata ids: Q856361 and Q577668). This dossier ends the Uzbek empire at its Cliopatria end (1511, after Shaybani's death on 2 December 1510) and the Khanate of Bukhara dossier opens at 1512. The colour agent may treat them as one family (both 'mongol').
Repair round ia-03-b (2026-10-19): Babur's 1511 capture of Samarkand and Bukhara added (loss to timurid-empire, mirror of timurid-empire /ledger/48; the Babur page dates it 1511 and gives no month, so the 1511 keyframe drops both cities); the 1497 found event now has kazakh-khanate as counterpart (Kazakh Khanate page, division c. 1495-96, mirror of kazakh-khanate /ledger/5, which is dated 1496); a 1510 loss of the steppe north of the Syr Darya to kazakh-khanate added at confidence 1 (the Kasym Khan page names the land and no year; mirror of kazakh-khanate /ledger/6). Not settled: the Syr Darya steppe's exact boundary (the Kazakh Khanate page names cities only; the 680 cells are Cliopatria's); who held Fergana and Khujand in 1497-1502 and the year of their loss (Babur page: Babur 'resigned all hopes of recovering Fergana' by 1502; Khujand unmentioned; timurid-empire dates the Fergana loss 1501, this dossier 1502 from Cliopatria); the Herat page is silent on the 1507 southern tongue.
Previously not settled: the holder of Tashkent in 1500-1503 (reviewer ia-03-b: the Moghulistan page names Mahmud Khan of western Moghulistan, the eastern-chagatai-khanate dossier, losing Tashkent in 1503; Cliopatria's Kazakh shape of 1497-1501 also touches Tashkent); the southern tongue of the 1507 shape (Birjand, Zabol) which no opened page supports (the Herat page was opened and is silent); Cliopatria's Timurid row has no Samarkand or Bukhara in 1497-1506 although the pages say Shaybani took them from the Timurids.
The Khanate of Bukhara dossier opens at 1512 with a found event that takes all of Transoxiana from shaybanids and a Samarkand contest dated 1512 from the Khanate of Bukhara page ('Samarqand was briefly lost to Babur in 1512'); the Babur page dates his capture of Samarkand and Bukhara to 1511, so that dossier should take the two cities from timurid-empire in 1512, not from shaybanids.
The Timurid dossier (ia-02) should know: Cliopatria's Timurid shape for 1512-1515 (3.2 M cells including Samarkand, Bukhara, Tashkent) runs three years past Babur's expulsion at Ghazdewan (1512).
